severity_rationale: C4 Low/QA: view-function inaccuracy. C4 guidance explicitly states 'Unused view functions (QA at best)' and even for used views, inaccuracy without a direct funds-at-risk attack path maps to Low. pendingReward is mandated by spec (item 10) and is used by integrators, but the inaccuracy only understates realized rewards (never overstates them, so no one is tricked into claiming more than they have earned). OTC mispricing requires a willing counterparty and off-chain trading infrastructure outside the protocol's control. No direct theft of funds, no protocol function impacted — just an informational discrepancy.
title: pendingReward view does not simulate dispatcherHook.pull() inflow, understating realized rewards and enabling OTC mispricing
description: pendingReward(account) computes pending rewards using the current on-chain rewardRate, windowEnd, rewardBudget, and accRewardPerShare, plus an in-memory accrual extension up to min(now, windowEnd). It does not simulate the dispatcherHook.pull() that stake/unstake/claim will trigger via _syncBudget, and does not fold in dispatcherHook.mintDebt() as a hypothetical inflow. When mintDebt is non-zero and would push candidate above rewardRate (triggering the reset branch and raising the rate), pendingReward underestimates the reward the user will actually realize on the next interaction. After windowEnd, pendingReward returns accrual under the pre-pull state rather than the post-pull state.
attack_path: UX / information-asymmetry surface rather than a direct attack: 1) User queries pendingReward() to decide whether to claim or to price an OTC sale of their staking position. 2) dispatcherHook.mintDebt() is non-zero and would, on pull, bring candidate > rewardRate; rate would reset upward. 3) Displayed figure understates actual claim payout. 4) A counterparty offering to buy out the staker's position at pendingReward captures the hidden upside. Magnitude is bounded by hook.mintDebt() at query time multiplied by the queried user's share fraction — meaningful on pools with long gaps between pulls.
impact: Inconsistent view vs mutation semantics. Frontends/integrators relying on pendingReward as a single source of truth display misleading figures that diverge from actual claim outcomes. Enables OTC mispricing of staking positions.
recommendation: Mirror totalDebt()'s pattern inside pendingReward: peek at dispatcherHook.mintDebt(), apply _applyAsymmetricWindow logic in-memory, and return the post-hypothetical-pull pending. Alternatively, expose a separate pendingRewardSimulated() that includes the simulation and keep the existing view simple, while documenting that pendingReward is pre-pull and realized rewards may be higher.

sanitization.rationale: Root cause is the pendingReward view implementation in NFTStaker.sol. Note: C4 universal-invalid rules say 'Unused view functions (QA at best)' — pendingReward IS used (it is spec-mandated per feature item 10), and the finding is NOT about it being unused, it is about it being incorrect relative to the mutation path. Keep; classifier may rate as low/QA given magnitude.
